KEY FACTS: rev = mol/s x price x 2.88e7. Prizes if separated purely: C6 paraffin mix (970 mol/s) ~$1186M; C5 mix (695) ~$618M; nC5 alone $438M; C6 naphthene mix $396M; nC8 $358M; C4 mix (544) $186M; C3 mix (286) $73M. 95% purity needed, 99% => 1.2x. Blends pay 85% of mean price.
Volatility gaps: C3/C4 ~30K, C4/C5 ~28K (easy); C5/C6 ~14K (moderate); C6 paraffin/naphthene ~3-11K (hard); C6/C7 ~18K (easy).

LESSON: columns here are extremely expensive ($120-390M/yr each) and my quick attempts never achieved 95% purity, so revenue was always ~0. A profitable plant needs revenue >> $300M/yr, i.e. at least a sharply-cut C5-mix-scale product. I lack the solves to build that tree.

PLAN: revert to the empty (reward 0.000) design — it beats every negative column design I evaluated — and finish at 0.
